Brilliant game, one of my favourites of all time.

First let's start with...

[b]The single player campaign.[/b]

You play as a Captain of the Space Marines, who are some of the mightiest heroes of the Imperium of Man. And you can tell, not just from how powerful you are in combat, but from the way the world reacts to you - you are high status, and your presence brings hope. My favourite moment was when a wounded Imperial Guard guy slumped against the wall whispers "I got to see a Space Marine before the end" in almost religious awe, followed by a prayer to the Emperor to aid you. Really makes you want to go out and kick Ork a[b][b][/b][/b]ss for the little guys.

Now not everything works exactly according to the Codexes; for example, Titus (your character) starts with a pistol and knife instead of a Captain's usual loadout. This is just usual shooter progress, of course; you pick up more weapons as you progress and this is fine.

But for the most part, the way the game represents Warhammer 40000 is clearly a labor of love. Everything is massive in size, gothic, the way it should be on a Forge World. Love that crane the size of a skyscraper. :) There's never an infodump about W40k lore, but the background is filled with these little things that you'll notice if you pay attention. Like the automated announcements playing in abandoned factories and population centers, that have a vaguely creepy "1984" feel to them, letting the unfamiliar but observant audience know just what kind of a world and what kind of a Universe this is. My favourite is "If you are injured, return to your quarters; the Machine God will watch over you". In the middle of an Ork invasion slaughtering everyone. Very helpful, I'm sure.

So yeah. There have been some crappy games based on the 40k licence, but this isn't one of them. Relic's Dawn of War was a good example of treating the subject matter correctly, and so is Space Marine.

As to just how badass this game can make you feel in combat, just watch TotalBiscuit's review of the demo. His unstoppable glee makes me smile.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nb50aAFiOpM

[b]Multiplayer[/b]

I spent more hours on the single player campaign than I'd like to admit, but it is the multiplayer that cemented this game as one of my very favourite games ever. Your abilities in it are scaled down for balance, of course - the jump pack in SP was overpowered as hell, and therefore only available for short segments of the campaign, but here it's a lot less destructive.

The combination of fluid melee-and-ranged combat, with all these wonderful Warhammer 40k weapons, and the possibility to play as an Assault Marine/Raptor, makes this literally my favourite multiplayer game that exists right now. It's just so much fun. Thunder Hammers and Meltaguns and Lascannons are powerful tools, but even the humble Bolt Pistol - my preferred ranged option - is a potent threat in the hands of a competent player.

If you're going to play Assault Marine, btw, check out my intro to the subject:
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=389736663

[b]State of the Multiplayer[/b]

So as not to mislead - the multiplayer playerbase is small now, especially since Eternal Crusade came out and drained some people. That's why public games only happen in Seize Ground, which is the point capture mode, on classic maps (which is fine, because it's the best mode and the best maps). Also, currently it's harder to get games in European mornings; the multiplayer picks up in the afternoon and evening. Nevertheless, games happen every day and there's lots of fun to be had.

[b]Downloadable content[/b]

I got the DLCs and don't regret it - playing as the Dreadnought is awesome beyond description - but be warned: for the most part you won't get to play them. You'll only play the DLC maps in private games, duels or arranged games with friends. Make lots of friends, invite 40 people at once and you'll get a 4+ vs 4+ game. There's also Exterminatus (not the best name for co-op mode), which gets a more difficult version in the DLCs, and that one's quite fun too.

But you can get by just fine without buying them, since it's classic mode that keeps getting public games.
